newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real falls 0.06 pct under new miniband.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real falls 0.06 pct under new miniband.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.06 percent to close at 1.0591 real per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank set a new mini trading band for the currency, dealers said.

Earlier today, the Central Bank set a new trading level for the real by buying dollars at 1.0565 reais per dollar and selling dollars at 1.0615 reais per dollar, signalling a 0.28 percent devaluation if compared to the previous mini-band of between 1.0535 and 1.0585 reais per dollar which was set on March 11.
The adjustment surprised the market which was expecting the Central Bank to lower the mini-band by between 0.10 or 0.15 percent.
Some traders said this move could mean the Central Bank intends to speed up the rate of devaluation of the real against the dollar currently in place.
Others, however, saw the Central Bank action as a preventive move previous to the Easter holidays next week.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real also dropped 0.30 percent to end at 1.0620 real per dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real fell 0.65 percent to end at 1.090 real per greenback.
